statements.body: Five families share a recurring school pickup run and currently coordinate via informal morning text messages.
The coordination method is described as frantic, implying it is unreliable or stressful under time pressure.
The desired output is a shared roster that shows which family drives on which day.
The system must support swapping turns between families, at minimum for reasons of illness or travel.
The five families are a fixed, closed group for the foreseeable future; the roster does not need to accommodate frequent membership changes.
How far in advance the roster is generated and whether it repeats on a fixed cycle or is built ad hoc each week.
What confirmation or acknowledgement is required when a swap is proposed and accepted.
Which platforms or devices the five families are expected to use to access the roster.

concerns.coverage: Families coordinating a shared school pickup via last-minute texts causes stress and unreliability; the pain is felt by all five families every school day morning without this project.
Five families are the operators and beneficiaries; all are peers with equal standing; no administrator role or scale beyond this closed group is stated.
Work enters as a scheduled driving turn; the key handoff is a swap request triggered by illness or travel, but who initiates, who approves, and how confirmation flows is not yet defined.
The roster (who drives which day) is the core data object; swap history is implied but not specified; retention period, export needs, and what must never be lost are unstated.
No scope exclusions are stated by the user; none can be inferred safely without risking silent assumptions.
No observable success criterion is stated; a hypothesis would be that families stop using morning texts and swaps are confirmed without chasing — but this is unconfirmed.

candidates.body: When a family cannot drive their day, what exactly should happen: who do they propose the swap to, who must accept, and how does everyone else learn the roster changed?
candidates.whySelected: The swap is the core interaction that replaces the frantic texts, and the ledger explicitly flags the confirmation flow as undefined; the first vertical slice cannot be built or judged without knowing who initiates, who approves, and how the change becomes visible.

candidates.body: Does the driving rota repeat on a fixed weekly cycle, or does someone build it fresh each week?
candidates.whySelected: This is an approved unknown that determines whether the slice is a static repeating schedule with swaps layered on top, or a scheduling tool in its own right — two very different builds.

candidates.body: What devices and apps do the five families actually use day to day, and is there anything (like a shared group chat platform) they all already have?
candidates.whySelected: An approved unknown; platform reality is a hard environmental constraint that decides whether the slice is a web page, a bot in an existing chat, or a native app, and it is cheap for the user to answer.

candidates.body: A month after launch, what would you look at to know this worked — for example, morning texts about pickup dropping to near zero?
candidates.whySelected: Success coverage explicitly notes no observable criterion exists yet; without one, there is no way to judge whether the slice relieved the stated pain.

readyAdvice.why: The core interaction — the swap flow — is still undefined, as are the rota cycle and the target platform; any of these could reshape the first slice, so the seed is not yet sufficient to start building with confidence.
